segments.title: 第64章 白嫖顏竹笙
segments.content:
In the review section for *I'm Really Not a Star*, there were about four or five comments with similar questions.

—What song is "Annual Ring"?

It was normal for readers not to know "Annual Ring," because that song was the theme for the 2015 TV drama *The Journey of Flower*, which hadn't even been conceptualized yet.

The bad news was, when Li Luo was writing, he wrote this song into the story.

The good news was, it was just a small subplot and didn't have much impact on the main storyline.

Li Luo scanned the main text, the corner of his mouth twitching as he couldn't help but sigh.

The content in the book related to "Annual Ring" was very simple.

The protagonist knew a big-shot celebrity he had worked with before. This celebrity's new TV drama was about to be released, but he was still unsatisfied with the theme song.

Li Luo had no idea how many times he had written similar plot points before.

In short, through various coincidences, the protagonist casually came up with this song, "Annual Ring," which the big-shot celebrity happened to overhear.

One thing led to another, and the song was chosen to be the theme song.

But this wasn't the crucial part. The crucial part was that the protagonist would use this song to establish a connection with this big-shot, making it easier to advance the subsequent plot.

However, for the sake of logic, Li Luo had specially designed the plot of the so-called new TV drama. The gist of it was a xianxia romance about a love story between a tree demon that had lived for tens of millions of years and a flower bud that had just achieved human form through cultivation.

After all, if you only looked at the lyrics of "Annual Ring," with imagery like "tree root," "fingerprint," and "annual ring" forced in for the sake of rhyme, you really couldn't tell what the hell it was about.

As a diligent and responsible web novelist, Li Luo could only fabricate a tree demon to loosely connect with these words in the lyrics.

Of course, since none of this was the main storyline, it didn't really matter how he played with it, as long as it ultimately served to build a bridge between the protagonist and the big shot.

However, when Li Luo was writing it, because it was a minor subplot he had dashed off, the description of "Annual Ring" was only a few hundred words long, so he didn't specifically check if the song had been released yet.

In the flow state of immersive writing, a few hundred words might unconsciously fly by in just a few minutes.

Which resulted in this little blunder.

Some readers who liked listening to music while reading entertainment-themed novels had specifically searched for the song when they read this part of the story, but they couldn't find it.

So they all flocked to the review section to ask about it.

Web novels in this era didn't have the "this-chapter-comments" function yet, only a general review section, so the impact wasn't huge for now.

But as Li Luo looked at these comments, he initially wanted to hurry home, change this section, and substitute it with a theme song from a TV drama that already existed before 2014 to salvage the situation.

But as this thought occurred to him, he suddenly turned his head to look at Yan Zhusheng, who was getting ready to leave. Another idea inexplicably popped into his mind.

"Yan Zhusheng."

"Hm?" Yan Zhusheng, who was slinging her backpack on, heard Li Luo's voice and turned back, puzzled. "Is there something else?"

"Do you have other plans this afternoon?"

"I do." Yan Zhusheng held up her right hand and counted on her fingers. "Go home, listen to music, read a book, take a shower, sleep."

"...In that case, could I consult you about something?"

"Go ahead."

"I wrote a song, but I only have the melody for a guitar version. How can I record it according to proper standards?"

"Huh?" Yan Zhusheng was stunned for a moment when she heard this. "You wrote a song?"

"Yeah... I guess you could say that."

Confirming his answer, Yan Zhusheng looked Li Luo up and down. Thinking about how this guy had managed to master perfect pitch in just twenty minutes, writing a song didn't seem quite so surprising.

With this in mind, Yan Zhusheng nodded to herself, and after some thought, she turned and walked out of the classroom. "Then come with me."

"Where are we going?" Li Luo followed behind, closed the classroom door, and hurriedly caught up to Yan Zhusheng's footsteps.

"To my place," Yan Zhusheng said, turning her head.

"Huh?"

...

Three o'clock in the afternoon.

Li Luo followed Yan Zhusheng and took a taxi to a place he was very familiar with.

Yan Zhusheng's home, in a high-end residential complex near the South Metro Station in Yinjiang District.

"Slippers." After pushing the door open and entering, Yan Zhusheng got a pair of slippers for Li Luo, then changed into her own and walked into the living room.

Li Luo followed her into the house, looking at the familiar yet unfamiliar room, feeling a bit dazed.

Ten years later, Yan Zhusheng still lived here, but it must have been renovated by then. The current decor was slightly dated.

But in terms of the furniture layout, it was identical to how it would be ten years later.

"Come with me." Yan Zhusheng didn't linger in the living room, heading straight for the second floor.

Li Luo followed her up to the second floor and entered a room.

In the center of the room was a piano, surrounded by a miscellany of various musical instruments and equipment. It was clearly a small recording studio.

Yan Zhusheng walked to the wall, picked up a guitar, and handed it to Li Luo. Then she sat down at the piano herself, turned her head, and said, "Sing it. The song you wrote."

"Okay, sure."

Li Luo was far too familiar with this room and felt no nervousness at all.

In his past life, while learning guitar in this very spot, he had no idea how many times Yan Zhusheng had corrected his posture.

Returning to this old place now actually made him feel very relaxed.

He held the guitar and began to play.

"A circle is drawn into a fingerprint~"

"Imprinted upon my lips~"

"The bitter kiss of memory~"

"Is a tree root~"

Yan Zhusheng closed her eyes, listening intently as Li Luo played.

When the interlude passed, she opened her eyes at just the right moment and tried to follow Li Luo's rhythm. Her ten fingers landed on the piano, playing a melody in accompaniment.

After singing it through the first time, Li Luo looked at Yan Zhusheng. "Um... How is it? Is it okay?"

Yan Zhusheng glanced at him, got up and walked to some equipment in the corner, fiddled with it for a bit, then sat back down at the piano and simply said, "Again."

Hearing that, Li Luo's heart skipped a beat, recalling the memories of being dominated by Yan Zhusheng.

Once she entered teaching mode, Yan Zhusheng instantly turned into a cold and aloof teacher.

"Fine." Li Luo sighed and started playing the guitar and singing again.

After he had sung it four or five times like this, Yan Zhusheng finally didn't make him repeat it again. Instead, she got up and started fiddling with the various pieces of equipment nearby.

Li Luo went over to take a look but couldn't understand what she was doing.

"I've more or less figured out the basic melody," Yan Zhusheng said. "Write down the lyrics for me later."

"And then?"

"Then I'll think about the arrangement," Yan Zhusheng thought for a moment. "I might have to ask a few arrangement teachers for their opinions."

"Huh? Isn't that too much trouble for you?"

"It's no trouble," Yan Zhusheng shook her head. "It's quite interesting."

Seeing her somewhat enjoying herself, Li Luo understood a little.

When it came to anything related to music, Yan Zhusheng probably would never find it troublesome or boring.

"Then is there anything I need to do? About when will it be ready?"

"Next week at the earliest," Yan Zhusheng estimated the time. "Come to my place again next weekend. The arrangement should be more or less done by then."

"I have another song," Li Luo thought for a moment, then asked brazenly, "Do you think you could help with it at the same time?"

Such a great person to freeload off of could not be wasted.
